course_title: Mental Health & Justice & Working with the Community

learning_outcomes.description: Describe and advocate for the role of speech pathology within mental health and justice. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6, 1.7, 2.2, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1)

Explain the importance of therapeutic relationships and identify strategies to support engagement and effective communication when providing speech pathology services in mental health and justice contexts. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 2.1, 2.6, 3.1)
Describe the key characteristics of major mental health and neurodevelopmental diagnoses across the lifespan. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.3, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3)

Formulate person- and family-centred management plans to address social, emotional, behavioural, educational and occupational goals for people with communication and swallowing difficulties in the mental health and justice setting. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1-1.7, 2,5, 3.4)
Advocate for interprofessional practice in managing people with communication and swallowing difficulties in the mental health and justice setting. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 2.5, 2.6)

Reflect on your learning, self-management and supervision needs, and identify strategies to communicate these needs and work safely within your scope of practice in mental health and justice contexts. (SPA PS Domains/Standards PS 2.1-2.5)

assessments.task_description:
This in-semester theory exam assesses content taught in weeks 1-3, relating to the role of the speech pathologist in the management of children, adolescents and adults with communication and swallowing disorders within mental health and justice settings. It will also assess content related to mental health conditions and importance of interprofessional practice. The exam will encompass short answer, case-based questions. This paper-based exam will be held in the Thursday, Week 7 tutorial.

This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

assessments.task_description:
In this assignment, students will be introduced to a person with mental health needs and/or involvement in the justice system. Using the case information and initial assessment data provided, students will develop an Easy English assessment report and video-record themselves explaining the findings and recommendations to the client. The report and explanation should communicate the person’s strengths, communication difficulties and functional impacts in an accessible, supportive and person-centred way. A detailed task description will be available on the SPCH7233 Blackboard site.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools.

assessments.task_description:
This end-of-semester theory exam assesses content across the course (weeks 1-8), with a focus on planning and evaluating speech pathology management for children, adolescents and adults with communication and swallowing difficulties within mental health and justice settings. Students will apply and integrate their knowledge of person- and family-centred goal setting, intervention, therapeutic engagement, interprofessional collaboration and outcome evaluation. The exam will comprise short-answer, case-based questions, including a case involving an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person, requiring students to demonstrate culturally responsive practice. The exam will be delivered in Inspera Assessment and completed on your personal laptop on campus.

This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

learning_activities.topic:
Online Self-Directed Learning Modules

A recorded course introduction will be available on the SPCH7233 Blackboard site before the first teaching session. In addition, 10 online learning modules, comprising recorded lectures and associated learning activities, will be released across weeks 1–3 and 6–8. Each module is expected to take approximately 1.5-2.5 hours to complete, including the recording and associated activities, giving an estimated total of 11–22 hours of online learning, excluding the course introduction.

These self-paced modules explore the role of speech pathologists in child, adolescent and adult mental health and justice settings. Through case examples and applied activities, students will examine mental health and neurodevelopmental conditions, therapeutic relationships and client engagement, referral and case history, assessment, goal setting, intervention and outcome evaluation. The modules also address interprofessional collaboration, advocacy, systems approaches, and professional wellbeing, support and supervision for safe practice within these complex settings.

Students are required to complete each module before its corresponding tutorial, where they will apply and extend their learning through discussion and practical activities.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

learning_activities.topic:
Cultural Safety in Practice Module 3 and 4

Students are required to complete Modules 3 and 4 of the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Behavioural Sciences Cultural Safety in Practice modules, Cultural Safety in Health and Community Services. Module 3 explores culturally safe practice through critical reflection on power, privilege and communication, strengths-based approaches, and examples from health and community services. Module 4 applies this learning to authentic case studies, asking students to examine their assumptions, address power imbalances, build respectful partnerships, and identify actions that support culturally safe environments, self-determination, rights and dignity for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.


Learning outcomes: L02, L06

learning_activities.topic:
Weekly On-Campus Tutorials

Students will participate in two 2-hour tutorials per teaching week, as scheduled in the course learning outline. Tutorials use inquiry-based learning, case discussions and practical activities to apply and extend the online learning in mental health and justice contexts. Guest clinicians will contribute their expertise to selected sessions. Three tutorials will incorporate practice education preparation (PEP), focusing on transferring knowledge and skills to complex practice, self-management and self-advocacy, and effective communication. Students are expected to complete the relevant online learning before each tutorial and actively participate in discussions and activities.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06
